## Independent AI review — advisory (DR-033 §6)

**Reviewer** verdict:
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: changes
blocking: 1
summary: Gate checks `git config user.email`, not the effective author identity, so `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=… git commit` silently produces the exact unlinkable-author commit it exists to refuse.
findings:
- blocking packages/minspec/src/lib/template-registry.ts:1298 — The gate reads `git config --get user.email`, which is a proxy for — not the same as — the email git will actually stamp as the commit author. Git resolves the author identity as GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL > user.email > EMAIL > hostname fallback, so `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=ghost@nowhere.invalid git commit` passes the gate whenever user.email happens to be allowlisted, while authoring the commit under the unlinkable address the gate exists to refuse. That is an undocumented silent bypass sitting beside the doc…
- medium packages/minspec/src/lib/template-registry.ts:1296 — `git config --get minspec.allowedCommitEmails 2>/dev/null || true` swallows every nonzero exit, so ANY failure to read the key — not just the intended 'key is unset' (exit 1) — collapses to an empty allowlist and turns the gate off silently. A key populated with `git config --add` twice is the concrete case: `--get` on a multi-valued key does not return the whole list (unverified — I had no shell here to measure the exact exit code and output on this git version), so a user who adds a second ad…
- medium packages/minspec/tests/pre-commit-author-identity.test.ts:1 (and .githooks/pre-commit) — This repo sets core.hooksPath=.githooks, so the generated hook never runs here — the repo where the 87 ghost commits were actually measured remains ungated by this change. The commit body declares the .githooks mirror and the 'add the address as a verified email on the account' step as out of scope, which is legitimate for the file allowlist, but neither deferred item carries a filed issue number, so the follow-up exists only in prose. File them (or keep #1114 explicitly open and say so) before…
- low packages/minspec/src/lib/template-registry.ts:1300 — `for minspec_allowed in $minspec_allowed_emails` relies on word-splitting (intended) but is also subject to glob expansion, and the comparison is exact and case-sensitive, so `A@X.com` in the allowlist refuses a commit authored as `a@x.com`. Harmless for realistic addresses, but the scaffolded CLAUDE.md section should say entries are matched exactly (case included) so a user who hits it can see why.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

**Security** verdict:
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: changes
blocking: 1
summary: Gate checks `git config user.email`, a proxy — GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL/EMAIL override it, so the hook silently passes the exact ambient-identity case it was written for; plus an un-namespaced bypass var and an un-mirrored .githooks twin.
findings:
- HIGH packages/minspec/src/lib/template-registry.ts:1298 — The gate reads `git config --get user.email`, which is not the identity git stamps on the commit. Author email resolves as GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL > user.email > EMAIL > generated user@host. So `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=unlinked@x` exported in a container/agent session (the very scenario the comment at line 1283 cites) with an allowlisted `user.email` PASSES the gate while authoring the commit under the unlinked address — a load-bearing gate failing open on its motivating case (invariant 2). The inverse also …
- MEDIUM packages/minspec/tests/pre-commit-author-identity.test.ts:44 — `cleanEnv()` strips only MINSPEC_GATE_OFF and EMAIL_GATE_OFF, and every case configures identity via `git config user.email`. The env-var author path (GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL / EMAIL) is never exercised, which is why the HIGH finding above survives a green suite — and an ambient GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL in the CI container would additionally make the 'ALLOWS' cases pass for the wrong reason. Recommendation: delete GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL/GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL/EMAIL in cleanEnv, and add a case that sets an allowlisted …
- MEDIUM packages/minspec/src/lib/template-registry.ts:1295 — `EMAIL_GATE_OFF` is the only un-namespaced bypass in the scaffolded harness — every sibling is MINSPEC_GATE_OFF / MINSPEC_ALLOW_MAIN / minspec.* (see lines 1148, 1199, 1453). This template scaffolds into third-party repos, where a generic `EMAIL_GATE_OFF` already exported by unrelated tooling would silently disable a MinSpec gate with no signal. Recommendation: rename to MINSPEC_EMAIL_GATE_OFF (or MINSPEC_ALLOW_ANY_EMAIL) in the hook, the doc table at line 501, and the docblock at line 1124 bef…
- MEDIUM .githooks/pre-commit:1 — This repo sets core.hooksPath=.githooks, so the generated .minspec/hooks/pre-commit never runs here (asserted at pre-commit-protected-branch.test.ts:341-345). The new Stage 1 gate is not mirrored into the .githooks twin, so the defect that motivated #1114 — 87 commits authored under an unverifiable address in THIS repo — remains completely ungated here after this change. The commit message discloses the gap but names no filed follow-up issue, so it is a prose-only deferral. Recommendation: mirr…
- LOW packages/minspec/src/lib/template-registry.ts:1300 — `for minspec_allowed in $minspec_allowed_emails` is unquoted, so the allowlist undergoes pathname expansion as well as word splitting: an entry containing *, ? or [ is globbed against the repo root before comparison, silently changing the effective allowlist. Emails rarely contain those, and the sibling protectedBranches loop shares the idiom, so this is hygiene rather than an exploit. Recommendation: `set -f` around the loop (restoring with `set +f`), or iterate a quoted list via IFS.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

_Reviewer agent is read-only and credential-free; verdict enforced by the deterministic fail-closed gate (`review-decide.sh`). Advisory only — the human holds the merge keystroke (never-wrong / HITL)._

## 🤖 AI review — `ai-review:pass`

> ⚠️ **This PR modifies the AI-review machinery (`.github/`/`scripts/`) — the code review still ran; its honest verdict is `ai-review:pass` (above), but a human must review because a gate cannot certify a change to itself.**
>
> The code-review verdict is reported AS-IS — it is **not** masked as `ai-review:changes` (#596), so a genuine reviewer-requested change on a machinery PR still surfaces distinctly. Auto-merge is held by a SEPARATE human gate instead: the `needs-human-review` label, the `machinery-review-required` check, and `ready-to-merge` staying red (no SHA-bound pass witness is posted for a machinery PR).

### Reviewer
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Opt-in author-identity pre-commit gate is correct, fails closed when configured, off-by-default (invariant 3 safe), and covered by real end-to-end commit tests.
findings:
- low packages/minspec/src/lib/template-registry.ts (Stage 1 author identity gate, `git config --get minspec.allowedCommitEmails`) — If the allowlist is ever configured as a git multivar (two `git config --add` calls), `git config --get` errors and returns empty, silently disabling the gate entirely. Documented usage is a single space-separated value, so this is a minor footgun rather than a defect; `--get-all` (joined) would harden it. Non-blocking.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

### Security (code changed)
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Opt-in author-identity commit gate: no secrets, no new deps, no injection sink, and off-by-default so it respects blast-radius invariant 3 — no security issues found.
findings:
- low packages/minspec/src/lib/template-registry.ts (pre-commit hook string, Stage 1 identity gate: `for minspec_allowed in $minspec_allowed_emails`) — The allowlist is word-split unquoted, which also enables glob expansion; an allowlist value containing a shell metacharacter (*, ?, [) would be pathname-expanded against the cwd. Not exploitable — email addresses don't contain those chars and the git config is repo-owner-controlled (no privilege boundary crossed) — informational robustness note only, not blocking.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

### Architect (design / scope)
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Opt-in author-identity pre-commit gate is architecturally sound — off-by-default respects blast-radius invariant 3, fails closed/visibly per invariant 2, reversible so no DR needed, contract documented and tested.
findings:
- non-blocking packages/minspec/src/lib/template-registry.ts:1291 (Stage 1 identity gate) — The gate validates `git config --get user.email` but not the effective commit author, so `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=…` or `git commit --author=…` bypasses it undetected. Correct for the documented container-ambient case, but the prose ('refuse a commit whose author email…') claims broader coverage than enforced.
- non-blocking packages/minspec/src/lib/template-registry.ts:1104 JSDoc / doc table ~L484 — New gate introduces another commit-gating stage without a DR; acceptable under the <1-day reversibility rule and it threads DR-037/#1114 traceability, but reviewers should confirm no DR was expected for adding a scaffolded gate class.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

### Skeptic (evidence discipline)
```
REVIEW_VERDICT_BEGIN
verdict: pass
blocking: 0
summary: Every claim in the diff (opt-in default, live-identity read, whole-gate bypass, unmade-commit-on-refusal, real-hook integration) is backed by citable code or a real behavior test; no false signposts or vacuous tests.
REVIEW_VERDICT_END
```

_Independent fresh-context reviewers (`scripts/review-branch.sh`, no-tools agents reading the diff as untrusted data); each label decided by the deterministic fail-closed gate (`scripts/review-decide.sh`). Posted by `minspec-sdd[bot]` from CI — provenance is the App identity, verified here, not the label alone (#428, #342). Coverage `panel` — voters that ran: **reviewer + security + architect + skeptic**. The combined verdict fails toward `changes` if ANY voter requests changes._

…harness

GitHub links a commit to an account by matching the commit's author email
against that account's verified addresses. Measured on this repo: 87 commits
carry claude@harvest316.com, an email that is not verified on the harvest316
account, so GitHub can't link them and renders every cross-reference they
generate as "ghost mentioned this" in issue timelines.

Root cause: nothing validated the committing identity. The pre-commit harness
gates secrets, frontmatter, the DR index and RCDD root-cause, but never
asserted that user.email is an account-linked address, so a local identity
that shadows the account's real one (a container session's ambient email, in
this case) goes unnoticed until someone reads an issue timeline. This is the
same identity-ambiguity class flagged once before (a checkout's user.email
shadowing the linked one) and never gated.

Add an opt-in author-identity gate to the scaffolded pre-commit hook
(packages/minspec/src/lib/template-registry.ts, Stage 1): once a project sets
`git config minspec.allowedCommitEmails "a@x.com b@x.com"`, the hook refuses
a commit whose user.email doesn't match, naming the offending address, the
configured allowlist, and the exact fix command. Bypass: EMAIL_GATE_OFF=1.
Unconfigured — the default for every project this template scaffolds into —
the gate is a total no-op, so no adopter is affected without opting in
(constitution invariant 3, blast radius). Documented in the scaffolded
CLAUDE.md's Pre-Commit Checks section alongside the other gates.

Covered by new tests (pre-commit-author-identity.test.ts): off by default,
enforces a configured allowlist, honours a multi-address list, names the
offending email and the allowlist in the refusal, leaves the branch tip
unmoved on refusal, and both the dedicated and whole-hook bypasses work.

Scope, stated plainly: this touches only the shared scaffolded harness
(packages/minspec/ + tests/), per this agent's file allowlist. Two more
pieces close out the issue and sit outside that allowlist or this agent's
access entirely: mirroring this gate into this repo's own hand-maintained
.githooks/pre-commit (root-level file, outside packages/tests/scripts), and
adding the unlinked address as a verified email on the harvest316 GitHub
account (human, requires account access — GitHub re-links historical commits
automatically once it's added, no history rewrite needed). Neither is done
by this commit; the 87 already-ghosted commits are unaffected by it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.messageBody:
…e user.email proxy

Root cause: Stage 1 of the scaffolded pre-commit hook decided on `git config --get user.email`, a proxy that git's own author precedence overrides (GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL, which `git commit --author`, `--amend` and `-C` export to the hook, then author.email, user.email, EMAIL), so each of those produced a commit under an address the gate never read; the same stage read the allowlist with `--get` (only the LAST value of a multi-valued key) behind `|| true` (a read error became "gate off"), and iterated it in an unquoted, pathname-expanding `for` loop.

The fix, all in the Stage 1 shell of PRE_COMMIT_HOOK:
- The verdict reads `git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT` and parses its <email>, which is exactly the address git records. An author git cannot name refuses.
- The allowlist is read with `--get-all`. Exit 1 (key unset) keeps the gate off; any other failure refuses visibly instead of reading as unset (invariant 2).
- Entries compare literally under `set -f`, so `*@example.com` can no longer pathname-expand into the name of a matching file at the repo root.
- The refusal says where the rejected address came from. When git config holds a different address it names the override (GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL, --author, an --amend or -C keeping an earlier author) instead of telling the user to fix a config that is already right. Only that message reads author.email / user.email; the verdict never does.
- The gate stays opt-in and a no-op when unconfigured, including when no identity resolves (invariant 3; new test).

Measured on git 2.54.0, not assumed: `git config --get` on a multi-valued key exits 0 with the LAST value (the review expected a non-zero exit), so the observable defect was the first value being refused. `--author`, GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL, author.email, EMAIL, --amend and -C all reach the hook as GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL, and `git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT` reports each.

Tests: 11 new cases in pre-commit-author-identity.test.ts, each override paired with its converse. 10 failed on cb23a843 (the unresolvable-identity case on its message only, since the old hook already refused that state); the eleventh guards the off-by-default no-op. All 19 pass after the fix, under bash and dash. The suite now strips ambient GIT_AUTHOR_* / GIT_COMMITTER_* / EMAIL and shuts out global and system git config, because the gate now reads them. The scaffolded CLAUDE.md prose and the hook JSDoc describe the recorded-author check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
